data.title: War weapons from Cambodia seized in Trat
data.description: A smuggling suspect has been arrested and two AK-47 rifles, more than 24,000 rounds of ammunition and other items smuggled from Cambodia seized at a pier in Laem Ngop district of Trat province.

data.title: Flood-weary Nan braces for more rain on Sunday
data.description: Authorities are closely monitoring the Nan River basin as water levels begin to stabilise and recede in several areas, while preparing for more rain forecast to hit the flood-weary northern province on Sunday.

data.title: Bangkok finds more houses crowded with ‘pink card’ holders
data.description: Thirteen households across nine districts in Bangkok have been found to have at least 16 migrant residents with pink ID cards registered at each address, prompting authorities to launch case‑by‑case investigations.

data.title: Suspect held after body pulled from Benjasiri Park pond
data.description: A homeless man was arrested on Saturday morning after another man was found dead in a pond at Benjasiri Park in Klong Toey district of Bangkok.

data.title: Industrial waste fires in Rayong ‘violated human rights’
data.description: <p>The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) has found that repeated fires at an industrial waste storage facility in Rayong violated residents' right to a healthy environment and exposed gaps in factory legislation.</p>

data.title: American woman in Thailand held for son's abduction
data.description: <p>An American woman wanted for alleged parental kidnapping in the United States has been arrested in Bangkok after nearly two years in hiding with her son, Thai police said.</p>

data.title: New illegal waste dumping task force set up
data.description: <p>The Pollution Control Department (PCD) plans to establish a ministry-level task force to tackle illegal industrial waste dumping after links have emerged across several eastern provinces.</p>

data.title: Cancer screening centre planned at new MRT station
data.description: <p>The Transport and Public Health ministries have launched a project to turn space at an Orange Line station into a preventive health centre, making cancer screening more accessible by public transport.</p>

data.title: Man found dead in pond at Benjasiri Park in Bangkok
data.description: An unidentified man was found dead in a pond at Benjasiri Park in Klong Toey district of Bangkok late Friday night.

data.title: Vigilance stressed along Thai-Cambodian border
data.description: <p>Thailand has been closely monitoring the situation along the Cambodian border and remains on alert, said ACM Prapas Sornchaidee, director of the Joint Information Center on the Thailand-Cambodia Situation (JIC).</p>

data.title: House committee rejects Student Loan Fund top-up
data.description: <p>The House committee scrutinising the fiscal 2027 budget bill has approved the reallocation of 11.16 billion baht to nine agencies, rejecting a People's Party proposal to provide additional funding for the Student Loan Fund (SLF).</p>

data.title: Hospital discharges three Thais after Israel blast
data.description: <p>Three of the six Thai workers injured when an unexploded munition detonated in an orchard in Metula, northern Israel, have been discharged from hospital, Labour Minister Julapun Amornvivat said.</p>

data.title: Prachin Buri group threatens fresh protest
data.description: <p>The Strong Prachin Network is considering moving its protest to Government House unless the government formally confirms that Prachin Buri will not be included in the Eastern Economic Corridor (EEC).</p>

data.title: Survey finds arsenic in North rivers
data.description: <p>Arsenic levels exceeded safety standards at several locations in the Kok and Sai rivers, while severely harmful levels were detected at all monitored sites in the Ruak and Mekong rivers, the Pollution Control Department (PCD) said yesterday.</p>

data.title: Co-payment scheme boosts Thai spending
data.description: <p>A survey by the Trade Policy and Strategy Office (TPSO) has found that most Thais participating in the "Thais Helps Thais Plus (60/40)" co-payment scheme used their benefits to buy ready-to-eat food and essential household goods.</p>
